description:
Size a filter WITHOUT saving or spending anything. Returns two numbers, and the difference between them is the point.

- matched_leads: how many leads the filter selects.
- eligible_leads: how many of those would actually GAIN from the stages you named — i.e. are still missing at least one of them.

🔴 FOR A RUN, REPORT eligible_leads TO THE USER, NOT matched_leads. "Select 5,000, enrich 200" is the ordinary case, not an anomaly: most of a mature corpus has already been crawled and verified. matched_leads over-states the run every time, and it is eligible_leads that the record ceiling, the cost, and the runtime are all decided by. Quoting the bigger number is how a user is surprised twice — once by the bill they expected and once by the one they got.

🔴 FOR A READ QUESTION — "how many of my leads are X?", "which of my leads have Y?" — matched_leads IS the answer, and eligible_leads is not. stages is still required, so pass the stages you would run, but do not quote eligible_leads as "how many leads are X".

A CRAWLED LEAD IS NEVER ELIGIBLE FOR spidersite. A lead counts as a spidersite gap only while it has no crawl record at all, and every crawl.* field lives on that crawl record. So a condition that needs a crawl.* value (anything but is_empty) selects only already-crawled leads, and a spidersite-only run over it has eligible_leads = 0 by construction. That is the gate working, not an empty corpus — the internal source enriches GAPS; it does not re-crawl.

Free and repeatable: nothing is written, nothing is queued. Iterate here until the number is right, THEN create a selection.

exclude_without_website.description: Exclude leads with no website at all — a site crawl cannot help them. Defaults to true.

filter.description: The filter AST — a TREE, never a string. A group is {op:'and'|'or', conditions:[…]}; a condition is {field, operator, value}. `field` MUST be a key from list_bulk_corpus_fields and `operator` one that field's own `operators` list allows — anything else is a 422 naming what was wrong. Call list_bulk_corpus_fields FIRST; do not guess field names. A negation (is_not, is_none_of, has_none_of, ne, does_not_contain) also matches leads whose value was NEVER MEASURED, so it answers "not known to be X", not "checked and not X" — for the ad answer, add {field:'crawl.ads_verdict', operator:'is_not_empty'} to mean checked. Only meaningful for source_kind='corpus_query'.

job_id.description: Narrow to ONE job (one location) inside a campaign.

source_kind.description: 'corpus_query' (default — an arbitrary filter) or 'unenriched_run' (scoped to one past campaign/job via campaign_id or job_id).

stages.description: Stages the NEW run would enable: 'spidersite' (crawl the website), 'spiderverify' (verify emails), 'vayapin' (publish a PERMANENT public profile page). Eligibility is scoped to THIS set — a lead missing only VayaPin is still eligible for a VayaPin-only run. At least one stage must leave a trace in the corpus.

workspace.description: Tenant to target (cli_…). Omit to use the active/bound workspace. list_workspaces shows the options.

name: count_bulk_corpus_leads
